LESSON: WRITING 8.5.1 COMPOSITION WRITING: SELF-ASSESSMENT

Grade: SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade seven
Subject: ENGLISH
Strand: Strand 8
Topic 8.5: Writing 8.5.1 Composition Writing: Self-Assessment
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Writing 8.5.1 Composition Writing: Self-Assessment, part of Strand 8 in SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade seven ENGLISH.

Key inquiry question: Why is it important to assess writing? 2. How can one improve their composition writing skills?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Writing 8.5.1 Composition Writing: Self-Assessment together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Collaboration and collaboration: A learner participates actively in the writing activity when working in pairs, sharing

and assessing each other’s narrative composition.

● Learning to learn: A learner organises their learning while writing and assessing his or her narrative composition

before sharing with peers for assessment.

Values:
Integrity: A learner learns to be honest and truthful while assessing their own and other’s compositions.

Link to other subjects

French, German, Chinese, and Arabic involve narrative composition writing.

Suggested Learning Resources

Braille machine, braille papers, audio-visual clips
